steps.intent: Our objective is to keep the Council focused on an OPCW fact-finding investigation, avoid premature attribution to the Syrian Government, prevent military escalation, and reaffirm Syrian sovereignty and resolution 2401. The difficult points will be Western demands for attribution and a new investigative mechanism, as well as pressure for stronger punitive language; we need to secure at least nine votes while preserving language that protects Damascus from blame and military action.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports the Russian draft’s emphasis on Syrian sovereignty, the OPCW’s independent investigation and the need not to prejudge the Douma allegations. We ask that the text explicitly reject any threat or use of force against Syria outside the Charter and Council authorization, and that OP4 also warn against public accusations or military threats before the OPCW reports. With those changes, Bolivia can support the draft.
messages.China: China supports the Russian draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It clearly condemns any use of chemical weapons, calls for an objective OPCW investigation and avoids prejudging responsibility before the facts are established. China stresses respect for Syria’s sovereignty and urges all parties to avoid escalation and politicization. We can support the text as it stands.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire welcomes the Russian Federation's effort to keep the Council focused on an OPCW-led, independent investigation and on avoiding escalation. We can support the text if it expresses grave concern at the Douma reports and turns the 2401 follow-up into a concrete demand with reporting on humanitarian access. We urge the penholder to incorporate these points in the interest of Council unity and full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018).
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the balanced, non-prejudicial approach of this draft and its emphasis on an independent OPCW investigation. We ask that the Council expressly reject any unilateral threat or use of force against Syria and keep any accountability discussion within the OPCW and international-law framework. We also urge all parties to implement humanitarian pauses and medical evacuations without delay, in line with resolution 2401 (2018).
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports this draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It rightly demands an independent OPCW investigation, full cooperation and access, and reaffirms resolution 2401 (2018) without prejudging the outcome. We encourage the penholder to preserve Council unity and to ensure the OPCW and humanitarian provisions are implemented promptly.
messages.France: France condemns the chemical weapons attack in Douma in the strongest terms and cannot accept a text that treats it as merely alleged or fails to demand full cooperation by the Syrian authorities. We need an explicit condemnation, immediate and unfettered OPCW access, and a clear commitment to accountability, including an independent mechanism to identify perpetrators. France is ready to work on a robust text, but the current draft does not meet our red lines.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan thanks the Russian Federation for the balanced draft and supports its core approach: a prompt, independent OPCW investigation and no prejudgment. We propose only technical strengthening to safeguard the integrity of evidence and to reinforce that any accountability must follow verified OPCW findings. We also ask to reflect the Astana and Geneva tracks in the political settlement paragraph, consistent with resolution 2254 (2015). Kazakhstan remains ready to support a unified Council message that prevents escalation.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait thanks the Russian Federation for circulating the draft but cannot support the text as written. We need a clear condemnation of the reported Douma attack, an explicit demand that the Syrian authorities cooperate fully and immediately with the OPCW, and a credible accountability hook; humanitarian implementation of resolution 2401 must also be demanded, not merely reaffirmed. If these points are not reflected, Kuwait will abstain.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands supports clear condemnation of chemical weapons and the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, but we cannot support this text as drafted. The Council must demand full cooperation, in particular from the Syrian authorities, and must establish an independent mechanism to identify those responsible. We also ask for a shorter reporting timeline and immediate notification of any obstruction.
messages.Peru: Peru thanks the Russian Federation for circulating a draft and supports a unified Council response based on the OPCW's independent verification. The current text does not yet meet the gravity of the Douma attack: it must explicitly condemn that attack and provide for a credible mechanism to identify those responsible. We also need a clear demand for unconditional OPCW access, including by the Syrian authorities, and direct reporting of the OPCW findings to the Council.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support the Russian draft as drafted: it does not clearly condemn the Douma attack, it does not demand immediate and unconditional OPCW access, and it lacks an attribution mechanism. Our red lines are a clear condemnation of the 7 April chemical weapons attack, unfettered access for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, and an independent mechanism to identify and hold accountable those responsible. We also need a shorter OPCW reporting timeline and explicit reaffirmation of the implementation of resolution 2401 (2018).
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports the OPCW investigation and a clear condemnation of the reported Douma attack. The current text is not supportable because it uses alleged language, only calls upon access, and lacks any accountability mechanism. We need the red-line changes above: strong condemnation, mandatory and unconditional OPCW access, and a clear path to identify and hold accountable those responsible. We also ask that reporting be accelerated and that implementation of resolution 2401 be demanded.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support the Russian draft as it stands. It fails to condemn the chemical weapons attack, refuses to name the regime responsible, and does not demand immediate and unfettered OPCW access. We require the changes above, in particular on condemnation, access and accountability; without them we will vote against.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support the Russian draft as written. It fails to condemn the Douma attack clearly, treats the attack as merely 'alleged', and creates no mechanism to identify responsibility. We require a text that condemns the chemical weapons attack, establishes an independent attribution mechanism, and does not constrain Member States' ability to respond.

It rejects Western red lines on condemning the Douma attack as fact, singling out Syrian authorities, and creating an attribution mechanism, so France, the United Kingdom and the United States remain opposed.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): The current revision reflects Bolivia's core concerns: respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity, rejection of threats or use of force, and the need for an independent OPCW investigation without pre-judgment. We therefore support the text and urge that OP4 and OP5 not be weakened in any final compromise. Bolivia will oppose any attempt to turn the investigation into a pretext for unilateral military action.
messages.China: China supports the revised Russian draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It condemns any use of chemical weapons, calls for an objective OPCW investigation, and opposes unilateral military action or pre-judging the outcome, while reaffirming Syrian sovereignty and the need to implement resolution 2401 (2018). China urges all members to avoid politicization and to work for Council unity on this text.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire thanks the Russian Federation for revising the text and welcomes the inclusion of grave concern at the Douma reports and the 15-day reporting requirement on resolution 2401 (2018). We can support the draft if OP6 is strengthened to make clear that accountability must follow verified evidence through appropriate international procedures, and if OP4 no longer discourages legitimate public concern while still opposing military escalation. We also seek an explicit OP8 call on the Syrian authorities to ensure immediate, safe and unhindered OPCW and humanitarian access in Douma and Eastern Ghouta.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: The delegation of Equatorial Guinea supports the current text, which reflects the concerns we raised in the previous round, particularly the no-force clause, the integrity of the OPCW/CWC process and the need for humanitarian pauses and access. We welcome the balanced language calling for an independent investigation without prejudging its outcome, while reaffirming the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria and the full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018). Equatorial Guinea therefore supports the adoption of this draft.
messages.Ethiopia: The Ethiopian delegation supports the current text. It appropriately condemns any use of chemical weapons, preserves the integrity and independence of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, and calls for full cooperation and immediate access. We also welcome its emphasis on the full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the need to avoid escalation. We have no further changes to request.
messages.France: France cannot accept a text that fails to condemn the Douma chemical attack and that does not clearly demand the Syrian authorities’ full cooperation with the OPCW. The call on Member States to refrain from any threat or use of force is unacceptable and would undermine accountability. France will oppose this draft unless these red lines are met, including credible arrangements to identify those responsible.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the revised draft as circulated. We welcome the inclusion of our previous points on preserving the integrity and independence of the OPCW investigation, evidence preservation and the Astana and Geneva processes. We call on all Council members to maintain unity and avoid any action that could prejudge the OPCW’s findings or escalate the situation, while insisting on full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018).
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait appreciates the strengthened humanitarian provisions, but it cannot support a text that does not clearly condemn the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma or provide a path to accountability. We will therefore abstain unless OP1 explicitly condemns the 7 April attack and OP6 includes a request for an independent and impartial accountability mechanism. Kuwait remains committed to Council unity and to preserving the integrity of the OPCW investigation.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands cannot support this text as it stands. Our red lines remain an independent attribution mechanism and binding OPCW access, in particular for the Syrian authorities. We also ask you to remove language that constrains responses to chemical weapons use and to shorten the reporting deadline. If these changes are not made, we will vote against the draft.
messages.Peru: Peru appreciates the strengthened OPCW access and reporting language, but the current text still does not clearly condemn the reported attack in Douma nor provide a credible pathway to identify perpetrators. For Peru, an explicit condemnation and an independent investigative mechanism are essential to uphold accountability and the Council's credibility. We therefore cannot support the text as drafted and ask for these changes; we remain ready to work in good faith.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support the current text as drafted. It still treats the Douma attack as merely alleged, does not demand immediate and unfettered OPCW access, and replaces accountability with language that could shield those responsible. We need the red-line amendments above; with them we can work toward consensus, but as it stands Poland would oppose.
messages.Sweden: Sweden appreciates the strengthened language on implementation of resolution 2401, but the core deficiencies remain. We cannot support a text that does not clearly condemn the Douma attack and does not provide a credible path to accountability. We ask you to incorporate these red lines; otherwise Sweden will be unable to vote in favour.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK cannot support this text as it stands. It still equivocates on the Douma attack, fails to demand immediate unfettered OPCW access from the Syrian authorities, and rejects any credible attribution mechanism. These are red lines; without them the UK will vote against.
messages.United States of America: The Russian draft remains unacceptable: it fails to condemn the Assad regime's chemical weapons attack in Douma and instead creates a false equivalence that constrains the United States and other Member States from responding. We require explicit condemnation of the 7 April attack, full Syrian cooperation with the OPCW, and a new independent attribution mechanism. We also cannot accept language that seeks to prejudge or restrict our right to respond; absent these changes, the United States will oppose this text.

It is expected to fall short of nine votes and faces opposition from France, the United Kingdom and the United States.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supported the Russian draft in the last negotiation round and its foreign policy emphasizes sovereignty, non-intervention, and opposition to unilateral force. It would likely vote yes and explain its support for an independent OPCW investigation and humanitarian implementation.
reasons.China: China consistently supports independent OPCW fact-finding, opposes politicization and military escalation, and had already signalled support for the Russian draft. Voting in favour also aligns with China’s defence of Syrian sovereignty and its position against pre-judging chemical weapons allegations.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire had marked the OP6 language as a red line, and the Russian draft retained problematic pre-assessment language. Its actual vote on the Russian draft was against, consistent with supporting a credible, independent OPCW investigation and accountability.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supported the Russian draft in the last negotiating round and its emphasis on sovereignty, OPCW investigation, and avoiding unilateral force aligns with its position. It would vote in favour but is not expected to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia had signalled support and generally favours a fact-based OPCW process, de-escalation, sovereignty, and UN-centred diplomacy, making a yes vote consistent with its stated position.
reasons.France: France’s red lines—explicit condemnation of the Douma attack, a demand for Syrian cooperation with the OPCW, deletion of the no-force clause, and an accountability mechanism—were rejected. Voting against is consistent with France’s position that the Russian draft weakens accountability and constrains responses to chemical weapons use.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan had already indicated support for the Russian draft and its record favours OPCW investigation, Syrian sovereignty, non-use of force, and the Astana/Geneva political track. Voting in favour is consistent with its prior positions on Syria and its alignment in the Council.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait had requested a red-line explicit condemnation of the Douma attack and an accountability mechanism, which were rejected, making abstention consistent with its last-round position. Kuwait still supports OPCW investigation and full implementation of resolution 2401.
reasons.Netherlands: The Netherlands had made an independent attribution mechanism and stronger obligations on Syrian authorities red lines, and the Russian text rejected them while also diluting accountability and no-force language. Voting against matches its stated position and alliance with like-minded members.
reasons.Peru: Peru’s red-line requests for explicit condemnation and an attribution mechanism were rejected, so it cannot support the draft, but it abstains rather than opposing the OPCW investigation and humanitarian provisions. This matches Peru’s emphasis on accountability, international law, and Council unity.
reasons.Poland: Poland’s red-line requests for clear condemnation, robust demands on the Syrian authorities, and stronger accountability language were rejected by the penholder. As a strong supporter of the OPCW and accountability, Poland would oppose this Russian draft.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation is the author of the draft and would vote in favour to support an OPCW-led investigation while opposing prejudgment and unilateral force. A pre-vote statement reinforces its established position that facts must be established before action and that Syrian sovereignty must be respected.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden's key red lines on condemnation, full OPCW access and accountability were rejected by the penholder, and the draft was viewed as weakening the integrity of the investigation. Given its principled position against chemical weapons use, Sweden opposed the Russian draft.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK’s red lines demanded explicit condemnation of the Syrian regime and an accountability mechanism, both of which Russia rejected. Voting against aligns with the UK’s firm policy that chemical weapons use must not be treated with false equivalence or impunity.
reasons.United States of America: The Russian draft fails the U.S. red lines: it does not clearly condemn the Douma attack or attribute responsibility, and it retains the no-force clause Washington sought to delete. The United States would oppose it as an inadequate and diversionary response.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia (Plurinational State of) thanks the Russian Federation for presenting this draft and will vote in favour. We condemn any use of chemical weapons, and we reaffirm that responsibility must be established through an independent, objective and impartial investigation by the OPCW, without politicization or pre-judgment. We reject any threat or use of force against the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of the Syrian Arab Republic, and we call on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and to guarantee immediate, safe and unhindered access. We also call for the full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and medical evacuations. Bolivia supports this text because it prioritizes facts, diplomacy, respect for international law and the avoidance of further escalation.
before.China: Mr. President, China is deeply concerned by the reports of the alleged use of chemical weapons in Douma. China opposes the use of chemical weapons by any country, organization or individual under any circumstances. The facts must be established through a full, objective, independent and impartial investigation. The authority and integrity of the OPCW must be respected, and no party should prejudge the outcome or use this incident for political purposes. The draft before the Council calls for prompt OPCW investigation and full cooperation, while reaffirming Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and urging all parties to avoid further escalation. China believes it is balanced and constructive and will vote in favour of it. We call on all Council members to preserve unity, avoid actions that complicate the situation, and support a political settlement in Syria.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Mr. President, Côte d’Ivoire strongly condemns any use of chemical weapons and remains gravely concerned by the reports from Douma. We have engaged constructively in the negotiations in a spirit of compromise, and we fully support the prompt deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. However, the text before the Council does not fully preserve the integrity and credibility of the independent investigation, and it retains language that risks undermining accountability and could prevent the Council from drawing conclusions on the basis of verifiable evidence. We had also sought clear provisions requiring all parties, including the Syrian authorities, to facilitate immediate, safe and unhindered access for OPCW personnel and humanitarian convoys. Those essential elements are not reflected with the necessary clarity. Côte d’Ivoire will therefore vote against this draft. We call on the Council to remain united in support of the OPCW, in defence of the prohibition of chemical weapons, and in ensuring full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the protection of civilians and unimpeded humanitarian access in Douma and Eastern Ghouta.
before.Ethiopia: Mr. President, Ethiopia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We are gravely alarmed by the reports of the alleged use of chemical weapons in Douma. Ethiopia unequivocally condemns any use of chemical weapons, by any party, under any circumstances. We believe that the facts must be established promptly, independently and impartially through the OPCW, and we call on all parties to cooperate fully and to grant safe, immediate and unhindered access to the relevant sites. At the same time, we stress the need to respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of the Syrian Arab Republic and to avoid any action that could further escalate an already dangerous situation. We also call for the full implementation of resolution 2401 and for safe and unimpeded humanitarian access to all those in need throughout Syria.
before.France: France will vote against this draft resolution. The reported chemical weapons attack in Douma is abhorrent, and the use of chemical weapons is unacceptable wherever and by whomever it is committed. France has consistently demanded an independent, impartial and credible OPCW investigation, immediate and unhindered access to all sites, and accountability for those responsible. The text before us does not meet those requirements: it fails to condemn clearly the attack of 7 April, does not demand the cooperation of the Syrian authorities as it should, and introduces a so-called no-force clause that would constrain the Council’s ability to respond to the use of chemical weapons and to uphold its own resolutions. France cannot support a text that weakens accountability and the credibility of the Council. We remain fully committed to resolution 2401 (2018), to unimpeded humanitarian access, and to a genuine political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Kazakhstan: Mr. President, Kazakhstan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We condemn any use of chemical weapons, wherever and by whomever committed, and we support a prompt, independent, impartial and credible investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. The draft before us is balanced: it demands cooperation with the OPCW, calls for full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), and rightly urges all parties and Member States to refrain from prejudging the outcome, from public accusations and from any threat or use of force. Kazakhstan firmly upholds the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria. We also stress that the humanitarian access and medical evacuations required by resolution 2401 (2018) must be implemented without delay. The only sustainable solution remains a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under United Nations auspices, including the Geneva and Astana processes.
before.Kuwait: Mr. President, Kuwait is gravely alarmed by the reports of chemical weapons use in Douma. The use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere and under any circumstances is unacceptable and constitutes a serious violation of international law. Kuwait supports the prompt deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and calls on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to provide immediate, safe and unhindered access, to preserve all evidence and to ensure the safety of investigators. We also stress the urgent need for full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and medical evacuations. My delegation had hoped that this text would contain an explicit condemnation of the reported attack in Douma and a clear path toward independent accountability. Because these essential elements were not reflected in the draft before us, Kuwait will abstain. We remain committed to an independent and impartial investigation and to accountability for any use of chemical weapons.
before.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands fully condemns any use of chemical weapons and supports an independent, impartial OPCW investigation into the reports from Douma. We cannot, however, support this draft. It does not provide for an independent mechanism to identify those responsible, it weakens the obligation on the Syrian authorities to cooperate immediately and unconditionally with the OPCW, and it risks constraining this Council’s ability to respond to chemical weapons use. For those reasons, the Netherlands will vote against the draft.
before.Peru: Thank you, Mr. President. Peru condemns all use of chemical weapons, wherever and by whomever they are used, and strongly supports a full, independent and impartial investigation by the OPCW, with immediate, safe, unhindered and unconditional access to all relevant sites and persons. We abstained on this draft because it does not explicitly condemn the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma and does not provide for an independent mechanism to identify those responsible. Accountability must be based on verifiable evidence, and all parties must cooperate fully with the OPCW and implement resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and the protection of civilians.
before.Poland: Mr. President, Poland has consistently condemned any use of chemical weapons, and the reports from Douma are deeply alarming. The Security Council must speak with clarity and unite behind an independent OPCW investigation with immediate, safe and unfettered access, and it must insist on accountability. Regrettably, the draft before us does not meet those requirements. It fails to clearly condemn the chemical attack, treats the obligations asymmetrically, and risks constraining the OPCW’s work and prejudging its outcome. For these reasons, Poland will vote against this draft. We remain ready to support a text that unequivocally condemns chemical weapons use, demands full cooperation by the Syrian authorities, supports accountability, and calls for full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018).
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution it has submitted. We do so because the Security Council must respond to the deeply alarming reports from Douma through a prompt, objective, independent and professional investigation by the OPCW, in strict accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention and OPCW procedures. We reject any use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere and under any circumstances. At the same time, we firmly oppose attempts to prejudge the outcome of the investigation, to use the tragic events for political ends, or to justify unilateral military action against the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. The draft calls on all parties, including the Syrian Government, to cooperate fully with the OPCW and to ensure safe and unhindered access. We urge all Council members to support this balanced text and to allow the OPCW to establish the facts before any conclusions or actions are taken.
before.Sweden: Sweden will vote against this draft. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons; the reports from Douma are deeply alarming and must be investigated promptly, independently and impartially by the OPCW. Sweden has engaged constructively to make this text acceptable, including by seeking clear condemnation, full and unconditional access, and accountability. Regrettably, the draft before us fails to condemn the reported attack in the strongest terms, falls short on the demands for cooperation and accountability, and risks constraining the independence of the OPCW. The Security Council must not send a signal that chemical weapons can be used with impunity. For these reasons, Sweden votes against.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote against this draft resolution. It fails to condemn the Assad regime’s chemical weapons attack in Douma, it refuses to establish accountability for those responsible, and it creates a false equivalence between the perpetrator and the victims. The text also calls on all parties to refrain from any threat or use of force in a way that would shield the Syrian regime from the consequences of its violations and constrain the Council from responding to a clear breach of international law. The United Kingdom fully supports an independent and credible OPCW investigation, but this draft is not a serious response to the use of chemical weapons. We urge Russia to stop shielding the Syrian regime and to work with the Council on a text that condemns this atrocity and ensures accountability.
before.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft. The Security Council cannot treat the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma as an open question while the evidence points to the Syrian regime, and this text fails to condemn the regime’s responsibility or establish an independent mechanism to identify perpetrators. It also includes an unacceptable provision that would constrain Member States from responding to chemical weapons use and appears designed to shield the Assad regime from accountability. The United States will vote against this resolution.

after.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Mr. President, Bolivia voted in favour of this draft because it offered the only responsible path: a prompt, independent and impartial OPCW investigation, full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, and a clear rejection of any threat or use of force. My delegation deeply regrets that the Council has failed to adopt it. Once again, political calculations and pre-judgment have prevailed over the search for facts and diplomacy. Bolivia condemns any use of chemical weapons, by anyone and under any circumstances, but responsibility must be established by the OPCW and not by public accusations or military threats. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the Fact-Finding Mission and to guarantee safe, immediate and unhindered access. We also call for full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access, medical evacuations and the lifting of sieges. The Council must not allow the use of chemical weapons to become a pretext for unilateral intervention, which would violate international law and deepen the suffering of the Syrian people. Bolivia reaffirms its solidarity with the people of Syria and its commitment to a Syrian-led political solution in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Côte d’Ivoire: Mr. President, Côte d’Ivoire regrets that the Council was not able to unite today on a text that would have sent an unequivocal message against the use of chemical weapons and in support of a credible, independent and impartial OPCW investigation in Douma. We voted against the draft because, in our assessment, it did not sufficiently preserve the integrity and credibility of the investigation, did not clearly require all parties, including the Syrian authorities, to provide immediate, safe and unhindered access, and retained language that risked weakening accountability and the Council’s ability to act on the basis of verifiable evidence. Côte d’Ivoire condemns any use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere and under any circumstances. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and to ensure the safety and security of its personnel. We also call for the full and immediate implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of all sieges and safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access, including medical evacuations. The Council must overcome its divisions and speak with unity and clarity. Côte d’Ivoire remains ready to work constructively towards a text that condemns chemical weapons use, demands full cooperation and accountability, preserves the integrity and independence of the OPCW, and supports the Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254 (2015), while respecting the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria.
after.Equatorial Guinea: Thank you, Mr. President. I take the floor to explain the vote of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. We regret that the Council was unable to adopt this text, which we considered balanced and constructive. Equatorial Guinea unequivocally condemns any use of chemical weapons, by any party and under any circumstances. Such acts are unacceptable and must never go unpunished. At the same time, we believe that the facts surrounding the reported incident in Douma must be established promptly, independently, impartially and credibly through the OPCW, in strict conformity with the Chemical Weapons Convention. We therefore supported the draft’s call for full cooperation with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, including safe, immediate and unhindered access to all relevant sites and persons, and for the preservation of evidence. Our vote does not prejudge the outcome of the investigation, nor does it align us with any party to the conflict. We firmly uphold the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and reject any threat or use of force against it. We also stress that all parties must avoid any action that could escalate tensions or undermine the credibility of the OPCW’s work. Equatorial Guinea further calls for the full and immediate implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities, the lifting of all sieges, and safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access, particularly in Douma and Eastern Ghouta. The humanitarian suffering of the Syrian people cannot continue. We urge all members of this Council to preserve unity, to act with responsibility and to continue to seek a peaceful and diplomatic solution to the crisis in Syria. Equatorial Guinea remains ready to support constructive efforts aimed at establishing the facts, upholding international law and alleviating the suffering of the Syrian people.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation regrets that the Security Council has not adopted our draft resolution. The text was balanced and constructive: it condemned any use of chemical weapons, demanded an objective OPCW investigation in strict accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention, called for full cooperation by all parties, including the Syrian Government, and rejected any prejudgment of the outcome or unilateral use of force. It also insisted on implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access.

It is telling that some delegations voted against not because the text lacked a demand for investigation, but because they have already appointed the guilty party. They tried to impose language that would prejudge the OPCW’s findings, create mechanisms outside the Convention, and prepare the ground for the use of force against a sovereign State. We cannot accept such attempts. The Russian Federation has consistently opposed chemical weapons use by anyone, anywhere. But we also reject the manipulation of the Douma tragedy for geopolitical ends.

We call on all parties to cooperate with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and to ensure safe and unhindered access. The Syrian Government has invited the OPCW, and we expect a professional and impartial investigation. We warn against any unilateral military action under a false pretext. Russia will continue to stand for the UN Charter, for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, and for a settlement based on facts rather than accusations.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President,

The United Kingdom voted against this draft, and we made clear why. It did not condemn the chemical weapons attack in Douma. It did not demand that the Syrian authorities cooperate fully and unconditionally with the OPCW. It did not establish accountability for those responsible. Instead, it sought to create a false equivalence between the victims and the perpetrator and to constrain this Council and Member States from responding to the use of chemical weapons. The Council cannot accept a text that gives comfort to a regime that has repeatedly used chemical weapons against its own people.

The United Kingdom strongly supports an independent, impartial and credible OPCW investigation into the reports from Douma. We call for immediate, safe and unhindered access for OPCW investigators and for all evidence to be preserved. Those responsible for chemical weapons use must be held accountable. There can be no impunity.

We regret that the Council has again been unable to send a clear and united message. We urge Russia to stop shielding the Assad regime and to work with us on a serious text that condemns this attack, demands full cooperation and supports accountability. The United Kingdom will continue to work with partners to uphold the Chemical Weapons Convention, to support the OPCW, and to ensure the full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and medical evacuations. The Council must not remain silent in the face of chemical weapons use.
after.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States voted against this draft because it was not a serious response to the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma. It failed to condemn the attack. It failed to establish accountability for those responsible. And it sought to constrain the ability of Member States to respond to chemical weapons use, while shielding the Syrian regime from the consequences of its violations. The United States fully supports a credible, independent investigation by the OPCW and insists that the Syrian authorities provide immediate, safe, and unhindered access. We also demand the full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and medical evacuations. But we will not accept a text that treats the victim and the perpetrator as morally equivalent or that turns this Council into an instrument of impunity. Russia can continue to shield the Assad regime, but the United States will not be silent. Chemical weapons use cannot be normalized, and those responsible must be held accountable.
